questions.q: (I, you and she) are the best brains here. (SSC Steno 13 Sep 2017 Shift 2)
questions.s:
The order of the personal pronouns 'I, you, and she' should be replaced by 'you, she and I'
For good and positive statements, the order is Second, Third, and First-person.

questions.q: My shoes were worn out so I had to buy a new one.
questions.s: (c) Explanation:- shoes plural me rakha jane wala noun hai isliye iske 'ones' pronoun ka use hoga. a/an articles plural se sath nhi aate aur yhan koi possession nhi bnana isliye baki options galat hain.

questions.q:
We have finished our work for the day, so let we go home early today.

[CHSL 11/08/2021 S2]
questions.s:
The correct answer is Option 2: let us go.

"Let" should be followed by the object pronoun "us" instead of the subject pronoun "we". So, "let we go" is incorrect and should be "let us go".

Correct sentence: We have finished our work for the day, so let us go home early today.

questions.q:
In the following question, some parts of the sentence may have errors. Find out which the sentence has an error and select appropriate option.

These tutorials are so elementary that they can help neither you nor I.

[CPO Tier II - 08 Nov 2021]
questions.s:
The incorrect part is: "neither you nor I"

Correct sentence: These tutorials are so elementary that they can help neither you nor me.

"Neither... nor" follows parallel structure, and the correct pronoun after "help" should be "me" (object form), not "I" (subject form).

questions.q: The principal objected (a) / to them wearing short skirts (b) / at the function. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s:
After a preposition like to, the possessive form should precede a gerund. Hence, their is correct instead of them.
Correct sentence: The principal objected to their wearing short skirts at the function.

questions.q:
My older brother,/ which you'll / meet later,/ is a dentist.

[CGL Pre 12/04/2022 S1]
questions.s:
Correct Answer: which you'll

The relative pronoun "which" is used for non-living things or animals. However, here it refers to "older brother", a person. The correct relative pronoun for a person is "who."

Correct Sentence: My older brother, who you'll meet later, is a dentist.

questions.q:
Her handwriting is definitely more beautiful than your.

(CGL Mains 03/02/2022)
questions.s:
Correct Answer: than your

The possessive pronoun "your" is incomplete here. It should be "yours," which is the independent possessive pronoun and is used without a noun following it.

Correct Sentence: Her handwriting is definitely more beautiful than yours.

questions.q:
Direction :- The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

There is none (A)/who can help you (B)/in this crucial moment of your career. (C)/No Error (D)
o: A
B
C
D
questions.s:
'who' के बदले 'that का प्रयोग होगा। वैसे सामान्य परिस्थिति में 'who' या 'which' के बदले ' that' का प्रयोग होता है।

याद रखें कि- All/ None/ Nothing/ only/ Superlative Degree Adjective / the same (के बाद यदि Verb का प्रयोग हो) आदि के बाद Relative Pronoun के रूप में सिर्फ 'that का प्रयोग होता है।

questions.q: He used to reply / that the only place / for which he went / was the town library. (SSC CGL Tier-01 01/12/22)
questions.s: For 'place', the relative adverb 'where' is more appropriate than 'for which'.

questions.q: Q6. 46. During the interview, she asked me <u>how many languages do I speak</u> fluently.
o: how many languages did I speak
how many languages does I speak
questions.s: Indirect question mein subject verb se pehle aata hai. In indirect speech, the subject precedes the verb in questions.

questions.q: Q14. Now it has finally dawned (a)/ upon her that one (b)/ should never compromise (c)/ with his dignity, integrity and self respect.(d)
o: A) Now it has finally dawned (a)
D) with his dignity, integrity and self respect.(d)
questions.s: When the subject is 'one', the corresponding possessive pronoun must be 'one's', not 'his'.

questions.q:
The investigation revealed that both of they had given false information to obtain the certificates.

(CGL Pre 12/04/2022 S2)
o: revealed that both of them
reveals that how they both
reveal that them both
questions.s:
The correct answer is: revealed that both of them

  • "both of they" is incorrect because "they" is a subject pronoun and cannot be used after a preposition like "of." Instead, the object pronoun "them" should be used.


Correct sentence: The investigation revealed that both of them had given false information to obtain the certificates.

questions.q: Q19. We thought (a)/ there was a good idea (b)/ to wear snow boots (c)/ before we stepped out.(d)
o: B) there was a good idea (b)
questions.s: The impersonal pronoun 'it' should be used as a dummy subject here. 'There' should be replaced with 'it'.

questions.q: Q24. Q[30]. Rex, the dog ______ belongs to Sam, is barking. [Bank Clerk 2023]
questions.s: Named pets take 'who'. नाम वाले पालतू जानवरों के लिए 'who' का प्रयोग करें।

questions.q: The woman which lives next door is a teacher.
questions.s:
For persons, we use “who”, not which.
So it should be: “The woman who lives next door is a teacher.”

questions.q: Q10. 42. People <u>like she and Rohan</u> should be encouraged to participate in the debate competition.
questions.s: Preposition 'like' ke baad objective case 'her' ka prayog hoga. Use objective case pronouns after prepositions like 'like'.

questions.q:
I sometimes pass a delivery man wheeling a large handcraft of japanese food. The cart bears a striking message: Creating a world where everyone believes in their own authenticity.

[СРО 16/03/2019 S1]
o: Creating a world whereas everyone believes in their own authenticity
Created a world where everyone believes in their own authenticity
Been created a world where everyone believes in their own authenticity
questions.s:
Correct answer: No substitution required

The given sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any substitution. The message on the cart, "Creating a world where everyone believes in their own authenticity," is appropriately structured. Here's why:

"Creating a world": The use of the continuous form "creating" is correct as it conveys an ongoing mission or effort.

"Where everyone believes": The pronoun "everyone" is singular, and the verb "believes" agrees with it.

"In their own authenticity": The use of "their" as a gender-neutral possessive pronoun is standard English usage, aligning with "everyone."

questions.q:
The master did not know who of the servants had broken the glass.

[MTS 14/8/2019 S2]
o: The master did not know
who of the servants
questions.s:
• "Since "servants" is a plural noun and we are referring to choosing from a specific group, the correct relative pronoun should be "which", not "who."

  • "Who" is used for people, but when referring to a specific member of a group or category.

  • Corrected Sentence: The master did not know which one of the servants had broken the glass.

questions.q:
There are some members who haven't paid his subscription yet.

[ CHSL 19/10/2020 S3]
questions.s:
Correct Answer: his subscription yet

  • The subject "members" is plural, but "his" is a singular possessive pronoun.

  • The correct possessive pronoun for plural "members" should be "their".

  • Corrected Sentence: There are some members who haven't paid their subscription yet.

questions.q: She stops herself her car at the intersection and looks both ways before proceeding.
o: She stops herself her car
at the intersection and looks
both ways before proceeding
questions.s:
The correct answer is: (a) She stops herself her car.

Keep, stop, turn, qualify, bathe, move, rest, and hide do not take a reflexive pronoun after them. In accordance with the rule provided verbs like "stop" do not take reflexive pronouns after them. Therefore, "herself" should be omitted from the sentence.

The corrected sentence is: "She stops her car at the intersection and looks both ways before proceeding."

questions.q: We must / take care of one other / in times of crisis. (SSC Selection Post phase-XI 27/06/23)
questions.s: The correct reciprocal pronoun is 'one another' (for more than two) or 'each other'.

questions.q:
Thomas is a man of word who have been paying back the borrowed money in instalments.

[CHSL 18/03/2020 S1]
o: Thomas is a man of word
questions.s:
Correct Answer: who have been paying back

The subject "Thomas" is singular, but the verb phrase "have been paying back" is incorrect here because "have" is used for plural subjects.

The correct verb should be "has" to match the singular subject "Thomas."

Corrected Sentence: Thomas is a man of word who has been paying back the borrowed money in instalments.

questions.q:
Now its referring to the same/big lug who met his fate/thanks to David's slingshot.

(SSC MTS 03/03/2023 S1)
o: Thanks to David's slingshot
Big lug who met his fate
Now its referring to the same
questions.s:
The erroneous part is "Now its referring to the same". The correct form should be "Now it's referring to the same".

  • "its" is a possessive pronoun (referring to something belonging to it), but here, we need the contraction of "it is".

Correct sentence: Now it's referring to the same big lug who met his fate thanks to David's slingshot.
